reasons.label: Verse not in this translation
reasons.explanation: The verse is not part of this translation’s text (a versification or textual omission).

reasons.label: Genealogy, census or record
reasons.explanation: A list, genealogy, census or record. There is no addressee to name.

reasons.label: Historical narrative
reasons.explanation: Narration of events with no direct address to the reader.

reasons.label: Legal or ritual instruction
reasons.explanation: Torah legislation or ritual instruction with no personal address suitable for naming.

reasons.label: Teaching without direct address
reasons.explanation: Teaching or exposition that does not address the reader directly.

reasons.label: Third-person wisdom saying
reasons.explanation: A proverb or saying in the third person. There is no addressee to name.

reasons.label: Poetry without address
reasons.explanation: Poetry with no direct address to the reader or worshipper.

reasons.label: Prophecy without address
reasons.explanation: Prophetic material with no direct address suitable for naming.

reasons.label: Apocalyptic vision
reasons.explanation: Apocalyptic vision or narration (Revelation, Daniel).

reasons.label: Collective address, no personal application
reasons.explanation: Addressed to a group, but not a promise, blessing or encouragement that could be framed for the reader.

reasons.label: Judgement, curse or warning
reasons.explanation: Personalising would turn a judgement, curse or warning into a personal pronouncement over the reader.

reasons.label: Words to a character in a narrative
reasons.explanation: Spoken to a specific person within a historical narrative (for example Jesus to Martha, God to Abraham). Naming the reader would change the audience.

reasons.label: Addressed to God
reasons.explanation: Prayer or praise addressed to God. The “thou” is God, not the reader.

reasons.label: First-person voice
reasons.explanation: The speaker’s own first-person words (psalmist, apostle, prophet). Inserting the reader’s name would change who is speaking.

reasons.label: Dialogue of Job
reasons.explanation: Speech within the dialogues of Job. God rebukes the friends’ words (Job 42:7), so their address is not the Bible’s address to the reader.

reasons.label: Song of Songs dialogue
reasons.explanation: Words between the lovers of the Song. A specific relationship that must not be re-addressed.

reasons.label: Rhetorical opponent
reasons.explanation: Address to an imagined opponent (“O man”, “thou that judgest”) in an argument.

reasons.label: Message to a specific church
reasons.explanation: Words addressed to a specific church or its angel (Revelation 2–3).

reasons.label: Curated context: not eligible
reasons.explanation: The curated Stage C passage context records this verse as not eligible for personalisation.

reasons.label: Divine speech to a people
reasons.explanation: Direct divine speech to Israel, Zion or a people. Whether a personal name may be inserted into God’s speech to His people needs theological review (Isaiah 43:1 is the reference case).

reasons.label: Covenant address to Israel
reasons.explanation: Torah address to Israel as a covenant people (“thou” is Israel). Collective; needs theological review before any personal framing.

reasons.label: Letter to a named individual
reasons.explanation: Written to a named person (Timothy, Titus, Philemon, Gaius, the elect lady). Personal address to the reader needs review.

reasons.label: First-person testimony
reasons.explanation: A first-person testimony or confession (for example Philippians 4:13). Whether it may be framed for the reader needs review; the speaker must not change.

reasons.label: Addressee unclear
reasons.explanation: The text alone does not show whether “thou” is God, the worshipper or someone else.

reasons.label: The Preacher’s address
reasons.explanation: Ecclesiastes includes the Preacher’s observations that are not all commands. Needs review before naming the reader.

reasons.label: Curated context: review required
reasons.explanation: The curated Stage C passage context requires review before personalisation.

reasons.label: Instruction to a young man
reasons.explanation: Proverbs 2:16–19 and 5–7 instruct a young man about adultery and marriage. Naming a reader of any gender would change its sense; needs review.

reasons.label: No safe insertion point
reasons.explanation: The addressee may be eligible, but no grammatically safe insertion point was found automatically.

reasons.label: Existing form of address
reasons.explanation: The verse already addresses a representative learner (“My son,”). The name follows that address, set off by commas. No word changes.

reasons.label: Wisdom address to the learner
reasons.explanation: Wisdom instruction addressed to a representative learner (“thou”, “thee”). The name is added as a direct address; no word changes.

reasons.label: Psalm addressed to the worshipper
reasons.explanation: The psalm addresses the worshipper (“thee”) and speaks of God in the third person. The name is added as a direct address; no word changes.

reasons.label: Encouragement to believers
reasons.explanation: A promise, blessing or encouragement to believers together. The text stays exactly as written; the name appears only in the title.

reasons.label: Corporate praise or confession
reasons.explanation: Corporate worship (“we”, “our”). The text stays exactly as written; the name appears only in the title.

reasons.label: Teaching of Jesus
reasons.explanation: Jesus’ teaching to His disciples or the crowds. The text stays exactly as written; the name appears only in the title.

reasons.label: Hand-authored rule
reasons.explanation: A hand-authored Stage B rule that inserts the name.

reasons.label: Hand-authored tracked replacement
reasons.explanation: A hand-authored rule using a tracked replacement (punctuation or minimal grammatical adjustment).

reasons.label: Open question for the supervisor
reasons.explanation: A hand-authored rule with an explicit open question for the theological supervisor.
